body.heading: Prepare your questions
paragraphs: Every family is full of stories that nobody has written down. Choose a storyteller — a grandparent, an aunt, or an older cousin — and prepare five questions.
Good starter questions: What was your favourite game as a child? What food did you love? Did you ever get into funny trouble?

body.heading: Hold the microphone
paragraphs: Sit together and hold your pretend microphone. Ask one question at a time and listen to the whole answer before asking the next.
Listening is the real job of an interviewer. Write down the best bits — the funny parts, the surprising parts.

body.heading: Keep the story safe
paragraphs: Stories disappear if nobody keeps them. Read your notes aloud so your storyteller can check you heard right.
You have just saved a piece of your family's history. That makes you a story keeper.

takeaway: Asking questions and listening carefully turns family memories into stories that are saved forever.
materials: A pretend microphone (a wooden spoon works)
safetyNotes: Interview someone your adult knows and trusts. If a question makes them sad, move on kindly to the next one.
screenFreeExtension: Retell the story you collected at dinner, in your own words, like a news reporter.
